text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Former prime ministers Omar Karami and Salim al-Hoss discussed the possibility of establishing an opposition front.
-Christian Maronite Patriarch Sfeir says: "The current situation does not satisfy anybody and we will work to change it".
-An opposition popular gathering calls the government to re-consider its audovisual law and license six more private television stations and 26 more radio stations.
-Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army militiaman was killed in a blast in south Lebanon.
-Central Bank says the foreign exchange reserves rose to $5.412 billion from $5.272 billion in mid-october.
-Bureau of teachers confirms a one-day strike on November 14.
-Israel's defence minister visits the occupied zone in south Lebanon.
-The ministry of interior says it will hand over to the constitutional court on Friday all documents related to appeals filed by candidates defeated in parliamentary elections.
-Syrian president Assad will receive former Lebanese prime minister Omar Karami today in Damascus.
-The new cabinet will be formed by Thursday.
